parts.note: a grand finale is a ..., and for a motorist that phrase is the crankshaft-side bearing of a connecting rod in a car engine

explanation.surface: A driver's spectacular closing flourish at the end of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Grande Finale' literally as a large terminal part: the motorist's version is the bearing that joins the connecting rod to the crankshaft.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the larger bearing of an engine's connecting rod, a part every motorist dreads hearing fail.

clue.text: "I was a King in, And you were a Christian slave" (Henley)

definitions.text: "I was a King in, And you were a Christian slave" (Henley)

parts.words: "I was a King in, And you were a Christian slave" (Henley)
parts.note: the missing word is the ancient city in W. E. Henley's poem 'To W. A.'

explanation.surface: A quoted line of verse with a place name left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley's poem begins 'Or ever the knightly years were gone... I was a King in ___'; the solver supplies the Mesopotamian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Mesopotamian capital on the Euphrates, famed for its kings and captives.

clue.text: The piano's in place for Sir Charles

parts.note: a grand is a piano, and the 's stands for 'is'
on means in position, as when something is on

explanation.surface: A piano is set up ready for a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Charles is the hero of Samuel Richardson's novel; 'piano's' gives GRAND plus IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Richardson's 1753 novel names its model gentleman hero by this surname.

clue.text: Undignified head, but old age rises after his assent

indicators.note: the old-age piece comes after the assent piece

parts.note: a nod signals agreement

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from bottom to top, so the old-age word is turned round

parts.note: eld is an archaic word for old age

explanation.surface: An elderly man nods his approval, losing his dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns ELD into DLE, which follows NOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial, humorous word for the head, too casual for dignified speech.

clue.text: Steward ready to produce mice plan

indicators.note: the letters of the two words stand ready to be worked into something new, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A household servant is poised to cook up a scheme against mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready to produce' asks for the letters of MICE PLAN to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A manciple was a steward who bought provisions for a college or inn, as in Chaucer's pilgrim.

definitions.meaning: melodies
shows off, as in airing opinions

explanation.surface: Music played for marching processions.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodies and showing off one's views publicly are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Bridge likely to show signs of shrinkage

definitions.meaning: the card game in its standard scoring form
to become smaller or narrower

explanation.surface: A bridge structure that seems to be getting smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard form of bridge and the verb meaning to shrink share the word.

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
the answer to clue 5 down, meaning tunes

explanation.surface: Gentle melodies for couples.
explanation.definitionFit: Two of a kind make a couple, so these are twosomes.

clue.text: Absorbing order to a lawyer's clerk?

definitions.meaning: taking up the whole attention; the verb form engages completely
an instruction to write out a legal document in a fair large hand

explanation.surface: A gripping instruction for a solicitor's assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: In law, engrossing a deed means writing out its final copy, the clerk's job.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy completely and to write a deed out formally are both senses of the verb.

definitions.text: for the Parson, 'Baccy for the Clerk" (Kipling)

parts.words: for the Parson, 'Baccy for the Clerk" (Kipling)
parts.note: the blank is the missing first word of a line in Kipling's A Smuggler's Song, naming a spirit run in by smugglers

explanation.surface: A line of verse with its opening word left out for the solver to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's A Smuggler's Song runs 'Brandy for the Parson, 'Baccy for the Clerk': the solver completes the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: The smuggled spirit in Kipling's poem is a distilled wine, a classic contraband liquor.

clue.text: Making a bang on the border ?

definitions.meaning: a bang is a straight-cut fringe of hair, so making one is cutting a fringe
edging or lying along a margin

explanation.surface: Causing an explosion right at the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a hairstyle's bang and forming an edge are both senses of the verb to fringe.

clue.text: A victory sign, love, to the vulgarian — O so fruity!

definitions.note: the answer is a fruit, while the clue word is an adjective

parts.note: V is the victory sign made with two fingers
love is zero in tennis, O
a cad is an ill-bred man

explanation.surface: Someone flashes a V-sign at a coarse fellow with fruity language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruity' defines loosely, describing the pear-shaped fruit the pieces build.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear-shaped tropical fruit with buttery green flesh.

parts.note: a boy's infatuation is the folk name of southernwood, a plant of the genus Artemisia

explanation.surface: A woman named Artemisia's first youthful crush.
explanation.walkthrough: Artemisia is not a woman but a plant genus; southernwood, Artemisia abrotanum, is popularly called by a name meaning a youth's affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Southernwood, a shrubby aromatic herb of the wormwood genus, carries this traditional country name.

parts.note: the conjuror's cry follows 'Hey', and it is also the musical instruction to play very fast, a tricky order for performers

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a request is hard to carry out.
explanation.walkthrough: Completes the magician's phrase 'Hey ___', and as an Italian tempo marking it is an order that is tricky to play.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjuror's word of triumph doubles as the Italian musical direction meaning very quickly.

parts.note: the heavy element is named after a planet, so it has astronomical connections

explanation.surface: A huge quantity of a radioactive element.
explanation.walkthrough: The element was named after the planet discovered shortly before it, hence 'astronomical'.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy radioactive metallic element named after the seventh planet.

parts.note: mavis is an old name for the song thrush, so its home is where the bird lays its eggs

explanation.surface: Somewhere a woman called Mavis lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Mavis looks like a woman's name, but it is a poetic word for the song thrush.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's home is the structure it builds to lay eggs and rear young.

parts.note: straw figures stand silently working in fields to frighten birds such as the Royston crow

explanation.surface: Quiet farm labourers in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royston crow is the hooded crow, named after the Hertfordshire town; field figures exist to frighten such birds away.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw-stuffed figures in fields do the silent work of keeping crows off the crops.

clue.text: Dogs are in a state of being coordinated

indicators.note: being in a state means being in disorder, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Dogs prove to be well coordinated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a state' signals that the letters of DOGS ARE IN are rearranged; 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged in order and working smoothly together, so coordinated.

clue.text: Knit less and get rid of wrinkles!

definitions.meaning: to reduce the number of stitches in knitting
to remove creases

explanation.surface: Do less knitting and smooth away age lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting the stitch count and taking creases out are both senses, the second a play on the prefix.

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
tending is looking after, giving care

explanation.surface: Struggling against worries.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to struggle or compete, so the participle means engaged in battle.

parts.note: the governing body of canons of a cathedral is also a section of a book, one of the parts that make up a book

explanation.surface: A churchman who takes bets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmaker' suggests a turf accountant, but a book is made of sections bearing this name, which is also a cathedral's body of clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral's body of canons and a numbered division of a book share the word.

clue.text: Little minutes make them mighty poetic

definitions.text: Little minutes make them mighty poetic

parts.words: Little minutes make them mighty poetic
parts.note: alludes to the hymn line 'So the little minutes, humble though they be, make the mighty ___ of eternity'

explanation.surface: Small stretches of time grow into grand verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Julia Carney's 'Little Things' says the little minutes make the mighty eternal periods; 'poetic' says the source is verse.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem, many small minutes add up to the long eras of eternity.

clue.text: Sound of commotion follows modest entry of a bad lawyer

indicators.note: the commotion piece comes after the modest piece

parts.note: shy means bashful or modest

indicators.note: the word for commotion is said and spelt differently in the answer

parts.note: a stir is a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A rowdy noise greets the shy arrival of a crooked lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of' makes STIR into STER, which follows SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: An unscrupulous practitioner of law who uses underhand methods.

parts.note: the spear-side is the male line of descent, so this is a kinsman through the father

explanation.surface: A family member armed with a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: The spear-side is an old term for the male line, as opposed to the distaff side.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman descended through the male line from the same ancestor.

definitions.meaning: the polar lights in the night sky, or the dawn
a girl's given name, also the Roman goddess of the dawn

explanation.surface: A woman who is not heavy, or not serious.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the glowing polar display and a woman's given name from the dawn goddess.

parts.note: in Poe's The Bells the bell is 'keeping time, time, time, in a sort of ___ rhyme'

explanation.surface: Resembling a poet's magical rhyming clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Poe's The Bells has the bells 'Keeping time, time, time, In a sort of ___ rhyme'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to ancient Germanic letters, with a sense of the mysterious and magical.

clue.text: Keenness displayed by those verbal jokers ?

definitions.text: Keenness displayed by those verbal jokers ?

parts.words: Keenness displayed by those verbal jokers ?
parts.note: a sharp tang, read as a word for a firm or agency of people making plays on words

explanation.surface: The eagerness that wordplay enthusiasts show.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PUN + GENCY, it suggests an agency of punsters; the whole word means sharpness or keenness of taste or wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpness of smell, taste or comment is the keenness the word describes.

definitions.meaning: required or obligatory
musth, the frenzied state of a male elephant

explanation.surface: An obsessive madness.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the frenzied rutting state of a bull elephant, also spelt musth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obligatory and an elephant's rutting fury both take this word.

clue.text: He keeps the drink under lock and key

definitions.text: He keeps the drink under lock and key

parts.words: He keeps the drink under lock and key
parts.note: a lockable decanter stand, named after the mythical king who could never reach the water before him

explanation.surface: A man who locks the alcohol away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'He' is the mythical king punished with drink just out of reach; his name is given to a locking stand of decanters.
explanation.definitionFit: A locked stand where decanters are visible but out of reach takes its name from the Greek myth.

definitions.meaning: a short-legged long-bodied dog used for hunting
the ... horn is a tenor clarinet

explanation.surface: A dog and a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged scent dog and a tenor clarinet both carry this name.

clue.text: Make a fuss once more, but have fun

definitions.meaning: create is British slang for making a fuss, and the prefix repeats it
to take recreation, amusing oneself

explanation.surface: Kick up a row again, yet enjoy yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'create' is British slang for making a fuss or complaining loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-create is to stir up trouble again, while recreate means to take leisure and enjoyment.

definitions.meaning: to put forward formally, as a bid
a boat attending a larger ship

explanation.surface: Proposing a little boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To submit a bid and a boat ferrying supplies to a ship share this word.
